notes: PSA 9.9 ng/mL. PI-RADS 2. PSAD 0.19. Prostate volume 50 mL. csPCa 0.66.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of persistently elevated prostate-specific antigen levels following a prior negative biopsy and recent multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging.

This 67-year-old delivery driver presents for urological follow-up after a marked rise in prostate-specific antigen from 2.5 ng/mL in August to 9.9 ng/mL in January. He lives alone but maintains close contact with his unmarried partner, who serves as his primary next-of-kin and accompanies him to clinic visits. His medical history is notable for hypercholesterolaemia managed with daily atorvastatin, and he is an ex-smoker with a 35 pack-year history who successfully quit in 2016. Lower urinary tract symptoms are mild, and he maintains a sedentary baseline punctuated by daily 20-minute walks, though a recent mobility limitation necessitates the use of a walking frame and a ground-floor consultation room. He consumes approximately one unit of alcohol weekly and recently completed a routine chest radiograph that showed no acute cardiopulmonary abnormalities.

Per rectum, the prostate feels smooth, symmetrical, and non-tender with preserved central sulcus, correlating with a clinical T stage of cT1c. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, clear respiratory fields, and regular cardiac rhythm. Abdominal inspection is unremarkable without palpable masses or organomegaly, and peripheral pulses are intact bilaterally.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
